title_en: Qi Yaochao, Yu Maoqing, and Chen Kezhi — case of fines and detention for obstructing execution of civil mediation
keywords_en: Civil; Obstruction of execution of civil mediation; First instance; Intermediate People's Court; Hubei Province; Legal person; Natural person; Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation); Transfer of sealed-up property; Obstruction of judicial execution; Partial support; Loan overdue; Mortgaged property; Seizure and transfer; Mortgage
full_text_en:
Qi Yaochao, Yu Maoqing, Chen Kezhi — Fines and Detention for Obstructing Enforcement of Civil Mediation Settlement

Person Fined: Qi Yaochao, Factory Director of Huangshi Chemical Fiber Knitting Factory, Hubei Province.

Persons Fined and Detained: Yu Maoqing, Deputy Factory Director of Huangshi Chemical Fiber Knitting Factory, Hubei Province.

Person Fined and Detained: Chen Kezhi, Worker of Huangshi Chemical Fiber Knitting Factory, Hubei Province.

Prior to February 20, 1989, Huangshi Chemical Fiber Knitting Factory, Hubei Province (hereinafter referred to as the Chemical Fiber Factory) had successively borrowed a cumulative total of RMB 352,000 from the Shihuiyao Office of Huangshi Central Sub-branch of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (hereinafter referred to as the Shihuiyao Office). Since 1987, the Chemical Fiber Factory had suffered consecutive years of production losses, rendering it unable to repay the overdue loans. The Shihuiyao Office filed a lawsuit with the Huangshi Intermediate People's Court of Hubei Province. After trial, the Huangshi Intermediate People's Court, on the basis of ascertaining the facts and distinguishing right from wrong, lawfully presided over mediation between the parties, and on April 20, 1989, a settlement agreement was reached: the Chemical Fiber Factory agreed to use its factory buildings and production equipment (net value of RMB 478,915.35) as collateral, and to repay the outstanding loans owed to the Shihuiyao Office in installments within three years from the date of the mediation agreement, with an annual repayment of over RMB 117,000, and loan interest of RMB 48,977.13 to be paid in full by December 20, 1989. If repayment was overdue beyond three years, the collateral property would be sold to satisfy the debt. However, by February 1990, the Chemical Fiber Factory had only repaid RMB 20,000 of the loan, and failed to perform the remaining due loans and interest in accordance with the agreement. In early 1990, the Shihuiyao Office applied to the Huangshi Intermediate People's Court for enforcement. The court found the application reasonable, issued an enforcement notice to the Chemical Fiber Factory, and also spoke with the relevant responsible persons of the factory, urging them to proactively perform the agreement according to law. However, the Chemical Fiber Factory refused to perform the agreement on the grounds of financial difficulties and inability to repay. During the process of supervising enforcement, the Huangshi Intermediate People's Court learned that the Chemical Fiber Factory was preparing to transfer by sale all of its collateral property, including factory buildings and production equipment, to other enterprises, and immediately went to stop it according to law. The Chemical Fiber Factory ignored the court's prohibition and transferred some property, including machinery, equipment, and office supplies, to enterprises such as Huangshi Children's Garment Factory and Citric Acid Factory. On February 4, 1990, the Chemical Fiber Factory continued to transfer the remaining property. Under these circumstances, the Huangshi Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 172, paragraphs 1 and 2, of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC (for Trial Implementation), and upon approval by the president, issued a sealing order, sealing the factory buildings of the Chemical Fiber Factory and the property that had not yet been transferred. On March 10, 1990, Qi Yaochao, Factory Director of the Chemical Fiber Factory, instructed Deputy Factory Director Yu Maoqing to lead more than ten workers to forcibly break the lock on the factory gate that had been sealed by the court and transfer the remaining materials to Hongguang Machinery Factory. Court enforcement personnel went to stop them upon being informed, but were besieged by Qi Yaochao and others. Worker Chen Kezhi claimed that the court could not control them and insisted on moving the untransferred property. By this time, all of the court-sealed property, except for the factory buildings, had been transferred.

In light of the foregoing, the Huangshi Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 77, paragraph 1, subparagraphs (3) and (4), of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation), which provides that if a participant in the proceedings or any other person transfers property that has been sealed by the court, or obstructs judicial officers in performing their duties by means of violence, threats, or other methods, or disrupts the work order of a judicial organ, the People's Court may, depending on the seriousness of the circumstances, impose a fine or detention, and upon approval by the president on March 11, 1991, decided to impose a fine of RMB 200 on Qi Yaochao, a fine of RMB 200 and detention for 15 days on Yu Maoqing, and a fine of RMB 200 and detention for 15 days on Chen Kezhi.

During the period of detention, the detained persons Yu Maoqing and Chen Kezhi admitted their mistakes and expressed their willingness to correct them. The Huangshi Intermediate People's Court decided on March 21, 1991, to release them from detention ahead of time.

Thereafter, the Chemical Fiber Factory repaid the loan to the Shihuiyao Office, and the dispute was resolved.
